body:
> I think the example is wrong because the figure element is not self-contained and can't be moved in the document flow without losing the meaning.

These are two very different things. Yes, it can't be moved. But it is still self-contained. There is no requirement that figure be arbitrarily movable.

> This paragraph also breaks the example:

That paragraph is saying something you _could_ do, _if_ you used certain structures, but not something that must _always_ be true for all figures.

> For completeness, the w3c specs says this:

There's a reason we don't include the "and that can be moved away from the main flow of the document without affecting the document’s meaning."---because it's not, in general, true about how figures are used.

> So... as a final question... what's the use case of figure with code inside? Apparently articles, documentation pages, and those things, can't make pieces of code as "self-contained units".

They definitely can. They're self-contained, just not able to be moved arbitrarily throughout the document. Those are two different concepts.
